text:
Neal Pionk is playing 24:18 a night for Winnipeg, the minutes of a top-pair defenseman, and he's been better with the puck than a year ago. Twelve points in 20 games matches his total from 51 games last season.

Some of that runs hot. He's shooting 8.2%, above our range for him, and his scoring rate (1.48 points per 60) is past even the top of the band we'd expect. But the Jets have also scored about five fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, so the luck runs both ways and his points haven't been inflated by teammates finishing everything.

The tracking explains the puck side. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones had him leaving the zone with possession on 65% of his exits last season and making 5.5 primary shot assists per 60, 81st percentile among defensemen. The defensive side is the worry. Evolving-Hockey had opponents gaining 0.14 expected goals per 60 with him on the ice, bottom 8% of defensemen, against tough competition.

He also hits (47 already). The Jets lost five straight and then won five straight across his last ten; he was steady through both.
